observation: The repository had package-owned skills, subagents, hooks, Recall prompt recipes, and agent-map commands, but no project-root instruction file that supported coding-agent hosts automatically load at session start. The installed release-set gate therefore proved that capabilities were projected without proving that a fresh agent was told to use them. This missing always-on router explains the common failure mode better than any individual map or hook defect: on-demand skills and commands existed, but nothing in the default project context connected ordinary task execution to them. Additional concrete defects amplified the symptom: the self-shape runner compiles Recall but explicitly withholds guidance judgement because it never reads system.md; the quick-start built agent-map only after workflow approve even though approve compiles Recall from map files that already exist; package-owned Git hooks could be installed while the repository had no tracked .agent-loop/githooks.json; and GitHub API/connector commits cannot execute local Git hooks in any case.

evidence.summary: The PR branch initially had no root AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, or GEMINI.md. Current Codex documentation automatically aggregates AGENTS.md into project instructions; Claude Code loads CLAUDE.md at session start and documents importing an existing AGENTS.md; Gemini CLI loads GEMINI.md and supports file imports. The repository therefore lacked the host-loaded entrypoint that could route an agent toward installed agent-loop capabilities.

The regression proves a canonical AGENTS.md router is created, Claude/Gemini use thin imports instead of copied guidance, project-owned text outside markers survives updates, unmanaged existing imports are preserved, malformed markers fail without rewriting the file, dry-run writes nothing, and install-assets projects the router automatically.

tools/self-shape-dogfood.php calls RecallOutcomeDraft::withholdInFile with the explicit reason that the harness never reads system.md. The installed release-set CI separately checks projected host files, so compilation/projection were being observed without agent consumption.

WorkflowApproveCommand passes map/search-index paths to Recall only when they already exist, while the previous docs/quick-start.md ordered workflow approve before map build. Building the map afterwards therefore could not influence the already-compiled briefing.

GitHookConfig defaults to an empty check list when .agent-loop/githooks.json is absent and PreCommitRunner exits successfully with 'No pre-commit checks configured.' The repository did not track that config and .gitignore ignored .agent-loop/* by default.

The regression creates a real Git repository with tracked hook policy and .gitmessage. Doctor first warns while core.hooksPath/commit.template are unset, then reports both integrations active after repository-local Git configuration is applied.

Acceptance-criteria and prompt-primitives candidate dogfoods, governed L2 execution-contract dogfood, installed release-set dogfood, and deterministic slop review run independently. Their separate results demonstrate that these gates exercise different capability planes rather than one end-to-end agent-host behavior.

hypothesis: Agent workflow integrations appear unused when on-demand capabilities are installed without an always-loaded project instruction router that tells the acting host when to discover and invoke them. Installation, deterministic compilation, host consumption, and local Git execution are separate capability planes: a skill cannot affect an agent that was never routed to it, Recall cannot consume a map built after compilation, and local Git hooks cannot run in a GitHub API write path.
validated_conclusion: Keep the always-on host context small and use it as a router, not a handbook. Project one canonical marker-owned AGENTS.md block that points non-trivial work at agent-loop status, installed skills, agent-map discovery, governed Contract/Recall state, and Git-hook boundaries; use thin host imports where the host requires CLAUDE.md or GEMINI.md. Make install-assets update that router idempotently so package upgrades can revise it without overwriting project-owned instructions. Separately classify dogfood evidence as installer, deterministic lifecycle, or agent-host behavior; build map/search evidence before workflow approval; distinguish compiled L2 prompts from briefing consumption; and report local hooks as not_exercised when the host bypasses local Git.
